### Observed differences

- The relative order of two groups of activities reversed. Before, A25 came before A20 in about 98 in 100 traces and A29 came before A20 in about 98 in 100; in the later window A20 came before A25 in about 97 in 100 and before A29 in about 99 in 100. The same full reversal appears for every tested pair between the optional trio A19/A21/A24 and the trio A20/A22/A23 (for example, A21 preceded A22 in about 33 of the roughly 36 in 100 traces containing both before, and A22 preceded A21 in about 28 of about 29 in 100 after). [REL016, REL021, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL030, REL031, REL033]
- Mean event positions moved accordingly: A20, A22 and A23 moved earlier (about 0.65 to about 0.39 of the trace), while A19, A21 and A24 moved later (about 0.37 to about 0.67). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]
- The successors at the boundaries of these groups changed: A19, A21 and A24 now lead to A30 in about 92–97 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions, where before they led to A25 in about 93–97 in 100; A20, A22 and A23 now lead to A25 (about 28–37 in 100) where they led to A30 (about 29–37 in 100). A40 now flows into A20/A22/A23 (before: A19/A21/A24) and A29 into A19/A21/A24 (before: A20/A22/A23). [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]
- Direct successions confirm this: A19→A30 and A21→A30 within one step, and A22→A25 and A23→A25 within one to three steps, are now common (each about 0 in 200 traces before, up to about 95 in 100 of observed pairs after, or about 200 traces for the A25 pairs); A21→A25, A22→A30, A23→A30 and A40→A21 within one step have largely disappeared (previously about 94–99 in 100 of observed pairs). [LAG018, LAG019, LAG020, LAG021, LAG022, LAG023, LAG024, LAG027, LAG028]
- A08 became rarer and later: it appeared in about 64 in 100 traces before versus about 29 in 100 after, its mean event position moved from about 0.26 to 0.41, and its dominant edge to A16 fell from about 93 to about 31 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (direct A08→A16 within one step fell from about 99 in 100 to about 43 in 100 of observed pairs). [OCC003, POS001, DIR002, LAG001]
- A04, A06 and A10 became more frequent, rising from about 7, 7 and 9 in 100 traces to about 21, 24 and 19 in 100, and their outgoing transitions now prominently include A46 and A15; A15 in turn continues to A16 in about 88 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (before about 61 in 100). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003, DIR005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Screening flagged 94 control-flow items where about 1 would be expected if nothing had changed, so the volume of flagged behaviour cannot be explained by random re-splits of a stable process [OCC001, OCC003, DIR002, REL023, LAG023]. The evidence supports the possibility that two segments of the process exchanged their relative order. Before, the segment running from A40 through A19, A21 and A24 into A25 executed before the segment running from A29 through A20, A22 and A23 into A30; in the later window the A29-led segment executes first and the A40-led segment after it. The supporting signs are direct and consistent: every tested cross-pair between the two groups flipped from one near-fixed order to the other, the position distributions shifted in matching directions by about a quarter of the trace, the successor choices at both segment boundaries changed accordingly, and the direct successions that appeared and disappeared match the new sequence. Co-occurrence between the groups stayed at about 29–39 in 100 traces, so the activities still execute together in the same traces; what changed is their order, not their participation in those traces [REL016, REL023, REL025, DIR006, DIR013, POS003, POS005, LAG021, LAG023].

Limitations: positions and lags are measured in event positions, not clock time, so "earlier" means earlier in the trace, not earlier in time. The evidence cannot distinguish a re-ordering applied within unchanged traces from a replacement of one ordered variant by another, and the order of the optional trio A19/A21/A24 relative to the rest is observed only in the roughly three to four in ten traces where they occur together; the evidence also cannot indicate why the order changed [REL016, REL021, REL023].

Other differences: A08 participation fell from about 64 to about 29 in 100 traces and it moved later, losing its dominant direct edge to A16; A04, A06 and A10 participation roughly doubled or tripled with new prominent edges to A46 and A15; and the long-standing successions A14→A15 and A45→A46 persist but weakened (about 98 to 80 in 100 of A14's outgoing transitions, and A45→A46 within one step from about 97 to 84 in 100). These changes may be connected to the reordering, but the evidence does not show how they fit together [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR015, LAG001, LAG030].

The instruction says: "A count many times larger cannot be explained by chance as a whole, even when all items describe one underlying difference; do not merge items for this comparison." So we proceed to judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

All items are control-flow family (OCC, DIR, POS, REL, LAG). No TWAIT, no resource items. So no time/resource discussion.
